g.text: Sources — Data centres: IEA, Key Questions on Energy and AI (April 2026): 485 TWh in 2025; roughly 950 TWh and just under 3% of

text.style: font-size: 7.9px; font-family: 'Georgia', 'Palatino Linotype', 'DejaVu Serif', serif; fill: #6e6e6e

g.text: global electricity by 2030. Global electricity generation 2025: ~31,700 TWh, derived from Ember, Global Electricity Review 2026.

text.style: font-size: 7.9px; font-family: 'Georgia', 'Palatino Linotype', 'DejaVu Serif', serif; fill: #6e6e6e

g.text: Water sector: ~4% of global electricity, IEA Water-Energy Nexus (WEO-2016 special report). Agri-food: ~30% of world end-use

text.style: font-size: 7.9px; font-family: 'Georgia', 'Palatino Linotype', 'DejaVu Serif', serif; fill: #6e6e6e

g.text: energy, FAO. Transport: ~29–30% of global final energy, IEA and REN21. Global energy supply: ~620 EJ (2023), Energy Institute

text.style: font-size: 7.9px; font-family: 'Georgia', 'Palatino Linotype', 'DejaVu Serif', serif; fill: #6e6e6e

g.text: Statistical Review, converted at 277.8 TWh per EJ. Checked 2 August 2026.

g.text: Method — The agri-food and transport bars are ranges because their published shares are of final energy, which is reported less

text.style: font-size: 7.9px; font-family: 'Georgia', 'Palatino Linotype', 'DejaVu Serif', serif; fill: #6e6e6e

g.text: consistently than electricity: the solid portion applies the share to total final consumption (~440 EJ), the pale portion extends it to

text.style: font-size: 7.9px; font-family: 'Georgia', 'Palatino Linotype', 'DejaVu Serif', serif; fill: #6e6e6e

g.text: total energy supply (~620 EJ). Data-centre figures are electricity only. The sector bars overlap one another — food-system energy

text.style: font-size: 7.9px; font-family: 'Georgia', 'Palatino Linotype', 'DejaVu Serif', serif; fill: #6e6e6e

g.text: already contains food freight and fertiliser — so they must never be summed. This is a comparison of magnitudes, not a budget.
